disadvantages: Current files and names are difficult for people to inspect and edit.
Extending the current copied hash fields would preserve needless maintenance.

alternatives.description: Read and write both JSON and TOML indefinitely.
disadvantages: Creates two live representations and ambiguous ownership.
Keeps conversion and divergence machinery in the shipped product.
rejectedBecause: The user waived a permanent converter or compatibility layer for Projector's one-time conversion.

alternatives.description: Use YAML for the human-authored source files.
disadvantages: Introduces a broader and less deliberately selected syntax surface.

assumptions: The executable typed contracts remain the sole schema authority.
Projector can package exact generated schemas and copy them into an adopting repository during initialization or preparation.
A maintained TOML implementation can round-trip every supported typed value on Node 24.
Machine-owned journals, receipts, external contracts, and derived SQLite state remain useful in JSON or SQLite rather than being converted for appearance.
payload.rationale: The user explicitly selected TOML on September 10, 2026 for human-authored Projector configuration and canonical artifacts, while retaining JSON for useful machine or external contracts and SQLite for suitable derived state. Readability includes stable identity-derived filenames, deliberate ordering, multiline prose, local versioned editor schemas, and ordinary edits that do not require manual fingerprint repair. Semantic hashes compare normalized parsed values; exact bytes remain separately bound only where reviewed mutation, executable input, or recovery requires equality. This authority selects a format boundary, not correctness, acceptance, provenance, authorization, or universal editor support.
